newsitem.title: GERMANY: German roaster Melitta aims at higher coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: German roaster Melitta aims at higher coffee sales.

text.p: German coffee roaster Melitta Kaffee GmbH said sales volumes in 1997 may exceed the 48,500 tonnes reached in 1996.
"We would like to achieve a slight increase in roasted coffee sales this year," managing director Hans-Guenther Hildl told a news conference on Wednesday.
The 1996 result represented a six percent rise over 1995.
Hildl said Melitta Kaffee had a 11.9 percent share of direct sales to consumers in the first quarter of 1997, compared with 11.4 percent in the same 1996 period.
Germany, which bought 9.4 million bags of green coffee in 1996, is the world's second largest coffee consumer after the United States. Melitta in 1996 was the fourth largest roaster.
Total sales in the German roasted coffee market in 1996 declined by 0.4 percent to 443,000 tonnes, according to data from coffee association DKV.
Melitta's sales revenue would only turn higher in the second half of 1997 when the effect of recent price increases would be felt, Hildl said.
Melitta sales last year dropped by 4.5 percent to 635 million marks because of lower retail prices.
Hildl said the company had still been profitable in 1996 but he declined to give details.
The German coffee division was also active in the emerging Greek roasted coffee market, where it accounts for 300-400 tonnes out of a total 2,000 tonnes a year.
Western and southern European sales represented nine percent of total volume and about five percent of sales revenue.
Attempted moves into the Czech Republic had been abandoned because of competitive pressures, Hildl said.
Overseas sales in Asia, Brazil and the U.S. are managed by the Melitta international coffee group, which is due to report its results in August.
